title: PC-CROP Federal Accounting — accountant organization-member context repair
purpose: Repair the proven authorization mismatch between the intended bookkeeper model (role=GUEST + job_profile=ACCOUNTANT/EXTERNAL_ACCOUNTANT) and the generic RLS transaction/controller fences. This slice opens only task-first accounting and Connection Center to an ACTIVE database-resolved organization membership with the required server-resolved capabilities. It does not weaken the generic GUEST denial used by unrelated contours.
boundaries: deriveTrustedRlsContext keeps rejecting GUEST; no global guest-role widening.

A separate organization-member transaction path requires authenticated user, session, tenant and organization and then proves ACTIVE membership with public.app_pc_crop_membership_id() inside PostgreSQL.
GUEST is admitted only on explicitly decorated accounting task/Connection Center handlers; all other AccountingController handlers retain the class role fence.
Task reads require accounting.dashboard.read resolved from durable membership job_profile/delegation; an unprofiled GUEST gets no accounting data.
Connection reads require integrations.read; attestation writes continue to require integrations.configure and MFA where already required.
No document, money, period-close, signature, provider, 1C runtime, EDO runtime, Prisma schema, migration, hosting or production mutation.
No browser-selected capability/job profile becomes authority.
Merge and green CI are not production acceptance.
requiredInvariants: Generic GUEST callers remain denied by withTrustedContext.
Organization-member context fails closed unless public.app_pc_crop_membership_id() returns an ACTIVE membership for current user/org.
GUEST + ACCOUNTANT can read task-first accounting but cannot gain one_c.configure or integrations.configure by role alone.
GUEST + EXTERNAL_ACCOUNTANT cannot configure integrations, close periods or reconcile merely because it can open the accounting work queue.
GUEST with no recognized job_profile receives no accounting task or connection read.
Cross-organization selection remains impossible because membership is resolved in PostgreSQL from current authenticated identity and organization.
